<P style="line-height:15.067px; margin:0px" align=center><B>TRANSCOMMUNITY FINANCIAL CORPORATION</B></P>
<P style="line-height:15.067px; margin:0px" align=center><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="line-height:18.667px; margin-top:0px; margin-bottom:-18.667px" align=justify><B>NOTE 23</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px; text-indent:72px" align=justify><B>DEFINED CONTRIBUTION PENSION PLAN:</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>TransCommunity has a defined contribution pension plan in the form of a 401(k) plan (the &#147;401(k) Plan&#148;) covering substantially all of its employees. &nbsp;Under the 401(k) Plan, employees can contribute pretax salary dollars subject to Internal Revenue Service ceilings. &nbsp;TransCommunity matches the up to 4% of salaries contributed by their employees and additionally contributes 5% of compensation regardless of what the employee contributes. &nbsp;Total expenses for the 401(k) Plan for the years ended December 31, 2006, 2005, and 2004 was $410 thousand, $554 thousand, and $370 thousand, respectively.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="line-height:18.667px; margin-top:0px; margin-bottom:-18.667px; padding-left:96px; text-indent:-96px" align=justify><B>NOTE 24</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:96px; text-indent:-24px" align=justify><B>SUBSEQUENT EVENTS</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px; padding-right:-2.4px" align=justify>On January 30, 2007, the holding company received an annual dividend of $300 thousand each from Bank of Powhatan and Bank of Goochland from each bank&#146;s reported 2006 net profits.</P>
<P style="margin:0px"><BR></P>
<P style="line-height:18.667px; margin-top:0px; margin-bottom:-18.667px; padding-left:96px; text-indent:-96px" align=justify><B>NOTE 25</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:96px; text-indent:-24px" align=justify><B>CORRECTION OF AN ERROR</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>On August 11, 2006, the Company concluded that the previously issued financial statements contained in the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-KSB for the year ended December 31, 2005 should not be relied upon because of errors in those statements. &nbsp;The Company discovered that it had incorrectly accounted for loans subject to certain loan participation agreements entered into with third-party financial institutions since the second quarter of 2004. During the second quarter of 2004, the Company implemented an automated loan documentation system which contained the option to include certain language that provided for termination of the participation agreement. &nbsp;This right to repurchase the participated balance allows the Company to retain a level of control over the loans sold to third parties. &nbsp;This termination clause allowed the originating institution to repurchase the loans sold to third parties and thus the loan transfers did not qualify for sale accounting treatment under SFAS No. 140, &#147;<I>Accounting for Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets and Extinguishments of Liabilities - a replacement of SFAS No. 125</I>&#148;. &nbsp;The Company had previously not reflected the participated balances of loans subject to these agreements on its balance sheet as required by SFAS No. 140. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>On January 22, 2007, the Company filed an amended Annual Report on Form 10-KSB/A for the year ended December 31, 2005.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="margin:0px"><B>NOTE 26 &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;LITIGATION:</B></P>
<P style="margin:0px"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>On June 14, 2006, an individual and a company controlled by the individual (Dean H. Gould and Cal-Flo Investments, LLC) filed a lawsuit against Main Street Mortgage &amp; Investment Corporation (&#147;Main Street&#148;), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bank of Powhatan, and five other defendants that are not affiliated with Main Street in the General Court of Justice, Superior Court Division, in Wake County, North Carolina. &nbsp;The lawsuit arises from three properties on which Main Street originated mortgage loans. &nbsp;The loans at issue were made by third-party lenders, and neither the Company nor any of its subsidiary banks hold any of the loans for its own account. &nbsp;The plaintiffs allege that the defendants developed a fraudulent scheme to originate these mortgage loans through Main Street employing, with Main Street&#146;s knowledge, inflated appraisals and other devices that resulted in damages to the plaintiffs in the aggregate amount of $100,000 to $150,000. &nbsp;The plaintiffs have requested both compensatory and punitive damages.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>Main Street filed an answer to the lawsuit and denies any liability. &nbsp;There has been no further activity in the lawsuit from any other party, and Main Street has ceased its business operations and filed for dissolution under applicable Virginia law.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>At the present time, the case is in the early stages, there has been no discovery, and accordingly, the Company, with advice from its legal counsel, cannot conclude on the outcome or estimate any potential loss.</P>
<P style="margin:0px"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>On November 2, 2006, James L. Minter filed a lawsuit against the Company and William C. Wiley, the former Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company, in the Circuit Court of the County of Powhatan in Virginia. &nbsp;Mr. Minter was a director of Bank of Powhatan, a subsidiary of the Company (the &#147;Bank&#148;) until January 12, 2007, when he was removed by the Company. &nbsp;He was a former director of the Company until his resignation on March 29, 2006. &nbsp;Mr. Wiley resigned as the Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer and from its board of directors in December 2005. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>The suit arises out of the Bank&#146;s purchase of Main Street Mortgage and Investment Corporation in early 2001. &nbsp;Mr. Minter alleges that in late 2000 Wiley withheld information concerning the value of Main Street Mortgage from the Bank&#146;s board of directors and that the Bank would not have acquired Main Street Mortgage if the valuation had been provided to the bank&#146;s board. &nbsp;The Company acquired the stock of the Bank in August 2001, several months after the Bank acquired Main Street Mortgage. &nbsp;Mr. Minter&#146;s suit claims that the Company aided and abetted and conspired with Wiley in his misrepresentation of Main Street Mortgage&#146;s value.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>In 2004 a committee of the Company&#146;s board of directors investigated the Bank&#146;s acquisition of Main Street Mortgage and concluded that Wiley had not defrauded the Bank&#146;s board and that any further action would not be in the Company&#146;s best interests. &nbsp;The committee reported its findings and recommendations to the boards of the Company and the Bank.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>Mr. Minter&#146;s suit also alleges that the December 2005 separation agreement between the Company and William Wiley improperly released claims the Company had against Wiley arising out of Wiley&#146;s alleged concealment of the Main Street Mortgage valuation from the Bank&#146;s board in late 2000. &nbsp;The Company believes that it never had a claim against Wiley in connection with the Bank&#146;s acquisition of Main Street Mortgage and that the separation agreement did not release any claim the Bank may have had against Wiley.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>Against Wiley, Minter alleges that (a) Wiley conspired to and engaged in a fraud on Minter by concealing and misrepresenting valuations regarding Main Street, (b) Wiley fraudulently induced Minter to invest in an entity unaffiliated with the Company and has engaged in conversion of certain of Minter&#146;s funds, and (c) Wiley breached his fiduciary duty to Minter, the Bank and the Company by concealing and misrepresenting valuations regarding Main Street. &nbsp;In the same proceeding, Minter has sued Wiley over a loss on an investment Minter made in 1999 in a business Wiley owned or controlled. &nbsp;The Company has had no interest in that business.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>Minter seeks unspecified rescissionary and compensatory damages, unspecified treble damages and punitive damages of $350,000 against each defendant, jointly and severally and with interest. &nbsp;Minter also seeks to recover his attorneys&#146; fees.</P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px; text-indent:24px" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>The Company believes, with advice from its legal counsel, insofar as it concerns the Company, Mr. Minter&#146;s suit is without merit.</P>
<P style="margin:0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0px; padding-left:72px" align=justify>The Company has moved for a dismissal; has brought claims against Mr. Minter for breach of fiduciary duty related to his use of confidential Company information for personal gain; and has removed him from the board of the Bank.</P>
<P style="line-height:15.067px; margin:0px" align=justify><BR>
